stem: A 13-year-old has nausea, abdominal pain, venous pH 7.25, point-of-care ketones 3.2 mmol/L, and blood glucose 12 mmol/L. What is the best interpretation?

options.text: This does not fit DKA because the glucose is below 14 mmol/L
This fits DKA because the triad is satisfied
This cannot be DKA unless ketonuria is also present
This is excluded because acidosis requires pH below 7.2
This is more consistent with uncomplicated hyperglycaemia

explanation: Diabetic ketoacidosis is the best interpretation here. The child meets the usual triad with hyperglycaemia, acidaemia, and ketonaemia.

citations.title: Louisa Leone MD3 2025 - Child and Adolescent Health - Study Notes.pdf

optionExplanations.A: Incorrect because the glucose threshold for DKA is lower than 14 mmol/L, and 12 mmol/L does not exclude the diagnosis.
optionExplanations.B: Correct because the triad is satisfied: blood glucose is elevated, venous pH is below 7.3, and ketones are 3 mmol/L or more.
optionExplanations.C: Incorrect because ketonaemia alone can satisfy the ketone criterion; ketonuria is not required.
optionExplanations.D: Incorrect because venous pH below 7.3 meets the acidosis criterion; pH below 7.2 is not required.
optionExplanations.E: Incorrect because acidosis plus significant ketonaemia is not consistent with uncomplicated hyperglycaemia.
